title: One exceptional blow-down over a finite-height valuation ring
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. Let $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ be a semistable $\eta$-modification. Write $B_f$ for the set of points $z\in Y$ such that, for some $t\in T$, $z$ is the generic point (its closure is the whole component) of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] $C_z$ of $Y_t$, and $f_Y(z)$ is a closed point of the entire scheme $X$, not merely of $X_t$. Call $z$ exceptional if $f_Y$ contracts $C_z$ to a point and, after base change to an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$, $C_z$ is $\mathbf P^1$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of the fibre in at most two points. If $z\in B_f$ is exceptional, there are a semistable $\eta$-modification $f_1:(Y_1,E_1)\to(X,D)$ and an $\eta$-modification $h:(Y,E)\to(Y_1,E_1)$ with $f_1\circ h=f$. The curve map of $h$ contracts $C_z$ to a point. For every $w\in B_f\setminus\{z\}$, $h(w)$ belongs to $B_{f_1}$, and $w\mapsto h(w)$ is a bijection $B_f\setminus\{z\}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{f_1}$, where $B_{f_1}$ is defined by the same closed-image rule relative to the unchanged target $X$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text:
Put $Z=C_z$ and $x=f(z)$. The semistable source $Y$ has geometrically reduced geometric fibres. Because $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ is normal integral and affine, [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal] applies to $Y	o T$: it gives that $Y$ is reduced and $\eta$-normal. The normalization $Y^
u	o Y$ supplied by [lem-trf-valuation-curve-projective-preparation] is a finite $\eta$-modification; by $\eta$-normality it is an isomorphism, so $Y$ is normal. Now [lem-trf-valuation-curve-projective-preparation] gives the finite normalization $X^
u	o X$ and, since the source $Y$ is normal, the unique factorization of $f$ through $X^
u$. Closedness of the image of a fibre generic point is unchanged by this finite replacement: a point above a closed point lies in a finite zero-dimensional fibre and is closed, and a finite morphism sends closed points to closed points. Thus the original set $B_f$ is unchanged. Work near the image of $Z$ in $X^
u$, localize $T$ beneath that point, and use the affine neighbourhood and normal projective compactification supplied by the preparation lemma. We now have a normal projective target, a normal proper source with geometrically reduced fibres, and a closed base point $s$ such that $Z\subset Y_s$. The restricted source and marking remain semistable near $Z$; outside that neighbourhood no semistability is asserted. We will construct an intermediate model that is an isomorphism wherever $f$ is an isomorphism, so the locality clause will return the diagram to the original $X$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.6, printed p. 32, first reduction paragraph

proof.text: The exceptional component is geometrically a projective line and its boundary in $Y_s$ has at most two branches. The polar-section lemma includes the descent $Z\simeq\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. Apply that lemma to obtain divisors $P_i$ through the other closed-fibre components, $P=m\sum P_i$, $L=\mathcal O_Y(P)$, and the sections $e=1$ and $a$. The value of $a$ is nonzero at every $p_i$, whereas the zero set of $e$ is $P$. Consequently their common zero set has empty closed fibre. This set is closed in the proper $T$-curve $Y$, so its image is closed in $T$; a nonempty closed subset of the spectrum of a local ring contains its closed point. Therefore the common zero set is empty.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.6, printed pp. 32--33, choice and lifting of the polar section

proof.text: The sections define a morphism $u:Y\to\mathbf P^1_T$ explicitly: on the open where $e$ generates $L$ use affine coordinate $a/e$, and on the open where $a$ generates $L$ use $e/a$; these functions are reciprocal on the intersection. On $Z$, the divisor $P$ is absent, so $a/e$ is a global regular function on $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. Such a function is constant: it is a polynomial in $t$ on one standard affine chart and a polynomial in $t^{-1}$ on the other, so their common Laurent polynomial has only degree zero. Thus both $f$ and $u$ are constant on $Z$. On each other component $Z_i$, $a/e$ has a pole of exact order $m$ at $p_i$, while being finite at its generic point; hence $u|_{Z_i}$ is nonconstant. It follows that the relative graph $(f,u):Y\to\mathbf P^1_X$ contracts exactly $Z$ among the components of $Y_s$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.6, printed p. 33, the relative projective-line morphism

proof.text: Restrict $u$ from the proper compactification to the preimage of the original affine neighbourhood. Its source and target still have their original smooth generic fibres. Normalize this restricted graph image, obtaining $Y\xrightarrow{h}Y_1\xrightarrow{f_1}X$ from the normalized-graph lemma. These are normal $\eta$-modifications with $f_1h=f$, and a component is contracted exactly when both $f$ and $u$ are constant on it. Thus among the components of the prepared closed fibre only $Z$ is contracted. The construction is an isomorphism wherever $f$ is an isomorphism, so projective preparation spreads and glues it back to the original diagram. Its support lies over generalizations of $x$. The other points of $B_f$ over $x$ are the other components of that same localized closed fibre, and are not contracted; those with a different closed image are outside this support. Hence, relative to the unchanged original $X$, $Z$ is the only component with closed image contracted by $h$. This does not assert that no component over a nonclosed point of $X$ is contracted.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.6, printed pp. 32--33, normalized image and return from the local projective setting

proof.text: On $Y_1$ take $E_1$ to be the schematic closure of $D_\eta$. The horizontal-curve-models lemma gives a multipointed curve and the $\eta$-modification $(Y_1,E_1)\to(X,D)$. Apply it also to $h:Y\to Y_1$: its generic marking has closure $E$, since the flat marking $E$ is the unique flat closed subscheme with that generic fibre. Thus $h:(Y,E)\to(Y_1,E_1)$ is an $\eta$-modification of pairs and the equality $f_1h=f$ holds also on markings.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.6, printed p. 33, define the marking accordingly; Remark 4.1 and Section 4.2

proof.text: Let $v$ be a closed point of $Y_1$ where $h$ is not an isomorphism, and let $t$ be its image in $T$. The graph lemma makes $F=h^{-1}(v)$ positive-dimensional and connected. It is supported on a closed subset of $Y_t$. This fibre is of finite type over the field $\kappa(t)$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; its closed subset $|F|$ is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Each one-dimensional component is an entire component of the pure one-dimensional curve $Y_t$, contracted by $h$. Properness of $f_1$ makes $f_1(v)$ closed in the original $X$. Step 4 therefore forces every such component to be $Z$, and $v=h(Z)$. Any remaining irreducible component of $|F|$ would be a closed singleton disjoint from $Z$ and from the other components: a point on another component would not be maximal irreducible. Since there are finitely many components, that singleton would be both open and closed in $|F|$, contrary to connectedness. Thus $|F|=|Z|$ and $F_{\mathrm{red}}=Z$ as reduced subcurves of $Y_t$. This argument imposes no condition on embedded associated points of $F$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.4.5, printed p. 32; Lemma 4.4.2 and Lemma 5.1(i)

proof.text: The local-criterion lemma applies at the point $v=h(Z)$ of Step 6: $Y_1$ is normal, $h$ is an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves, and every point of $F$ lies in the original semistable source. Its reduced subcurve is $Z$, which after geometric base change is one smooth projective line, with tree incidence graph and at most two boundary plus marking points by exceptionality. Hence $(Y_1,E_1)$ is semistable at $v$. At any other closed point $h$ is an isomorphism on a neighbourhood; uniqueness of the flat generic marking closure from Step 5 identifies the pairs there, so semistability is inherited from $(Y,E)$. Finally the semistable locus is open by the same criterion lemma. Its closed complement is empty: any nonempty closed subset of the quasi-compact scheme $Y_1$ has a closed point (a minimal nonempty closed subset exists by quasi-compactness applied to descending chains; the $T_0$ property then makes it a singleton). Thus $(Y_1,E_1)$ is semistable everywhere.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.4.5, printed p. 32; Lemma 4.4.2 and Lemma 5.1(i)

proof.text: Finally use the fibre-generic isomorphism clause of finite-fibre-valuation-domination for $h:Y\to Y_1$, whose target is normal with smooth generic fibre. Each generic point of a fibre of $Y_1$ has a unique preimage and $h$ is an isomorphism near it. Conversely, a noncontracted fibre component of $Y$ maps onto a fibre component of $Y_1$: its image is a closed irreducible curve in a pure one-dimensional fibre. Thus the fibre generic points of $Y_1$ correspond exactly to the noncontracted fibre generic points of $Y$. Under this correspondence $f_1(h(w))=f(w)$, so closedness in the original $X$ agrees in both directions. By Step 4 exactly $z$ is removed from the closed-image set. This gives the required bijection $B_f\setminus\{z\}\simeq B_{f_1}$ and the contraction and factorization already constructed give all the other clauses.

lean.statement: theorem valuation_exceptional_blowdown (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] (V : ValuationSubring K) [Finite (PrimeSpectrum V)] (X Y : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (hX : Smooth (pullback.snd X.x (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (hD : Etale (pullback.snd X.d (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (f : Y.Hom X) (hf : f.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype))) (hY : Y.IsSemistable) (t : Spec (.of V)) (C : Set (Y.x.fiber t)) (hC : C ∈ irreducibleComponents (Y.x.fiber t)) (z : Y.x.fiber t) (hz : IsGenericPoint z C) (hclosed : IsClosed ({f.curve (Y.x.fiberι t z)} : Set X.X)) (hexceptional : f.IsExceptionalFiberGenericPoint (Y.x.fiberι t z)) : ∃ (Y₁ : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (f₁ : Y₁.Hom X) (h : Y.Hom Y₁), f₁.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) ∧ Y₁.IsSemistable ∧ h.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) ∧ h.curve ≫ f₁.curve = f.curve ∧ h.marking ≫ f₁.marking = f.marking ∧ (h.curve '' (Y.x.fiberι t '' C)).Subsingleton ∧ Set.BijOn h.curve (f.closedImageFiberGenericPoints \ {Y.x.fiberι t z}) f₁.closedImageFiberGenericPoints
